key_insight: Self-improving agents need better learning signals, not just more failure examples. GEPA-Curator argues that curating which tasks inform prompt optimization can help avoid learning from misleading failures.
problem_solved: An agent can fail because of weak prompts, limitations in its execution setup, randomness, or noisy evaluation. Treating all failures as useful feedback risks ineffective or harmful prompt updates.
method: Build on reflective prompt optimization approaches such as GEPA, which learn from failed agent runs.
Curate the tasks supplied for learning rather than treating every failed run as equally informative.
Prioritize actionable feedback about prompt weaknesses over failures caused by execution or evaluation noise; implementation details are not available in the truncated abstract.
impact: For practitioners, the central lesson is to check feedback quality before using failures to improve an agent. Better task selection could reduce wasted optimization effort and misguided updates, although the provided abstract does not report measured results.
visual_elements: Failure-source diagram: prompt weakness, execution limitations, randomness, and noisy evaluation.
Curation funnel: failed runs → task selection → actionable feedback → prompt update.
Side-by-side workflows contrasting learning from every failure with learning from curated tasks.
Signal-versus-noise icons highlighting informative feedback and misleading failures.
paper_title: GEPA-Curator: Curated Learning for Self Improving Agents
paper_authors: Zack Yu, Nicholas Lee, Minjae Lee, Lakshya Agarwal, Luca Manolache
